item.title: Speculative Application
item.description: The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) is an award-winning international think-tank that aims to conduct cutting-edge independent research on European foreign and security policy and to provide a safe meeting space for decision-makers, activists and influencers to share ideas. We build coalitions for change at the European level and promote informed debate about Europe’s role in the world. In 2007, ECFR’s founders set about creating a pan-European institution that could combine establishment credibility with intellectual insurgency. Today, ECFR remains uniquely placed to continue providing a pan-European perspective on some of the biggest strategic challenges and choices Europeans need to confront, with a network of offices in seven European capitals, over 90 staff from more than 25 different countries and a team of associated researchers in the EU 27 member states. For more information check our website: ecfr.eu

item.title: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, London
item.description: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA), London This London-based role will support delivery of the PPCA Secretariat by coordinating events, steering committee and member engagement, and internal processes ensuring smooth day-to-day operations across the PPCA. Background The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview The PPCA Secretariat Coordinator plays a central role in supporting the effective delivery of the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) Secretariat’s work. The role coordinates events, member engagement, governance meetings and operational processes, ensuring smooth collaboration across a global network of governments, businesses and civil society partners. Working closely with the Secretariat Manager, Head of Secretariat and wider E3G teams, the Coordinator provides high-quality logistical, administrative and stakeholder support that enables the PPCA to advance its international mission and deliver impact across a fast-paced and dynamic policy environment. Key Responsibilities Lead preparation for key events Coordinate logistical preparation and delivery of PPCA events, including agendas, timelines, invitations and supporting materials. Manage event logistics such as venue liaison, travel arrangements and scheduling. Maintain and update the PPCA contact database, calendar and forward plan of key meetings and milestones. Conduct background research to support preparation of meetings, briefings and deliverables. Organise meetings and delegations with senior stakeholders Support coordination of meetings and delegations involving senior political, civil society and media stakeholders. Manage logistics including scheduling, travel coordination, agendas and briefing materials. Support the Head of Secretariat with meeting scheduling. Membership coordination Coordinate communication and engagement with PPCA members. Organise PPCA governance and member meetings, including PPCA Steering Committee, Implementation Committee and Members Meetings. Maintain accurate records of member contacts, engagement and correspondence. Work with the communications team and Secretariat Manager to coordinate progress updates on PPCA work. Operations and Internal Coordination Support the development of effective ways of working and communication for a growing Secretariat team based across multiple time zones. Support recruitment processes, including coordinating applications, interviews and candidate correspondence. Strengthen cross-team coordination by contributing to the development and maintenance of internal tools and processes that support events and Secretariat activities. Support drafting of internal documents, reports and correspondence as required. Provide updates on PPCA activities to E3G internal communications, ensuring PPCA updates are shared at staff forums and newsletters. Provide flexible administrative and coordination support to the Secretariat Manager as required. About You Motivated by E3G’s mission and keen to gain hands-on experience in policy-oriented research and stakeholder engagement in an international setting. Several years’ relevant professional experience and track record in a relevant setting. High level of initiative and be positive, organised, resilient, and able to deliver high-quality work on time. Skills & Experience Experience of events management. Experience of building relationships and networks, and working with partner organisations, coalitions, and networks including senior stakeholders. Experience of project and budget management. Prince 2 or other project management training or qualification would be considered relevant but not essential. Very strong written communication skills and advanced written and spoken English. What We Offer Permanent, full-time position. Work-life balance. Enjoy a 35-hour workweek with a hybrid work model and flexitime. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Pension contribution plan E3G offers a reward and benefits package which compares well with other organisations within our sector. The indicative salary range in the UK for this position is between £41,498 - £44,000, dependent on experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they have the right to live and work in the jurisdiction in which E3G employs them. Occasional international travel may be required from time to time. We are unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Your Application Please email your application in English and include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of maximum one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Recruitment Process First online interview with HR and Team Members Final interview with HR, Secretariat Manager, Head of the PPCA Secretariat The deadline for applications is July 31, 2026. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we will not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

item.description: Senior Communications Officer, PPCA, Singapore This post based in Singapore, to lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Who We Are The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview Lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Key Responsibilities Communication Strategy : Work with the PPCA Comms Team, the broader PPCA team, and with relevant governments (PPCA co-chairs: the UK and Canada; CTC co-chairs: France and Indonesia) to lead, develop and deliver comprehensive communication strategies that effectively communicate PPCA’s value proposition to our key target audience, closely following the political and media debates in Southeast Asia to identify where strategic communications can be usefully deployed in order to speed up the coal-to-clean transition. Messaging : Develop and refine compelling and impactful narratives that effectively address local priorities, concerns, and opportunities while creating a compelling vision of a prosperous, resilient future powered by clean energy. Identify regional proof-points and case studies, as well as leverage closed-door PPCA engagements to generate exclusive insights. Operationalise narratives with a wide range of communications material (e.g., press releases, press briefings, social media content, op-eds, blogs, communication support during events), ensuring consistency across all communication channels. Media Relations : Bring a strong understanding of the media landscape in Southeast Asia to the PPCA Team. Cultivate strategic media partnerships through consistent engagement, positioning PPCA and its spokespeople as a valued resource for regional energy transition insights. Proactively identify opportunities to engage the media and pitch stories, deliver media assets, develop speaking points and other supportive material for interviews. Stakeholder Engagement and Events : Establish new partnerships and leverage existing ones to refine and amplify messages and identify and elevate local influential voices in comms activities. Use social media to increase visibility and create and strengthen connections. Coordinate online or in-person events for the PPCA Team, co-creating the initial concept and seeing them through to completion. Support the PPCA team in representing the organisation at other relevant events to establish relationships and enhance the Alliance’s profile. Monitoring and Evaluation : Track and analyse the impact of PPCA’s communications efforts in Southeast Asia, including media coverage, social media tracking and stakeholder feedback. Provide regular reports to senior staff and funders on the effectiveness of communication strategies and identify areas for improvement. Contribute to the broader comms activities of the PPCA’s comms team as required. About You A strong track record of building and maintaining impactful media relations in Southeast Asia, including pitching stories and securing media coverage. An enthusiasm to embrace complex, technical topics, and transform them into compelling narratives about the benefits and feasibility of the energy transition. The versatile and adaptable skills necessary to flourish in a fast-paced and wide-ranging work environment and work across time zones. Capability to meet deadlines independently in fast-paced environments. Fluency in written and spoken English, our working language; additional languages are an asset. Skills & Experience At least five years of professional experience in leading external communications, including developing and implementing communication strategies. Proven experience in working in networks with a strong track record of leading on stakeholder management. Demonstrated ability to work with a diverse range of stakeholders, including governments, think tanks and financial institutions. Proven experience in delivering events. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan E3G is looking for a Senior Policy Advisor to lead analysis and engagement on trade diplomacy within its Japan programme. The new role will sit within E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team and will work closely with our Japan and trade experts to develop E3G’s work on the intersection of Japan’s trade policy, energy and economic security strategies, and climate objectives – with trade playing a key role as a diplomatic lever across these areas contributing to accelerating the clean energy transition. The role The role will build on existing work on trade and its use as a diplomatic lever, leading the development of strategies and engagements to align Japan’s trade, and economic policies, with the goals of a clean energy transition and ambitious climate action. The candidate will be based in Japan and will be required to work remotely. We are looking for an intellectually curious, enthusiastic person with experience of condensing and communicating complex information into clear, targeted analysis and advice for varied stakeholders. You will be motivated by building relationships with external stakeholders, and by creating impactful outcomes through strategic collaborations. You will have the opportunity to develop the strategy and shape the work programme, in consultation with colleagues in the Japan team and across E3G’s wider trade and industry related teams. Background E3G is an independent climate change think tank with a global outlook. We are world leading strategists on the political economy of climate change, dedicated to achieving a safe climate for all. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Delivering a rapid, managed transition of the global power system from coal-to-clean, not via gas, is a fundamental condition to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team mobilises diplomatic actors to drive real-world, real-economy progress on ending the global use of the coal power and transitioning to clean energy. E3G identifies opportunities for influence and interventions, collaborates with civil society campaigns and partners, and fosters international diplomatic alliances to create a world where no new coal is built, and where existing coal is replaced by clean, affordable energy to enable a climate-safe world. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic insight and thought leadership on trade and diplomatic engagement with Japan in the context of broader global climate and energy goals. Monitor and track developments relating to Japan’s trade relationships with a focus on key partner countries, including various bilateral and multilateral frameworks and agreements (e.g. FTAs), government strategies and publications (e.g. Green Transformation Strategy; and industrial policy priorities, such as the 17 Strategic Fields under Japan’s growth strategy etc.), as well as commercial drivers relating to both traditional and clean energy supply chains, in order to assess their impact on Japan’s energy and economic security priorities and identify opportunities for strategic interventions. Produce analysis, presentations, briefings and other materials, both internally to contribute to E3Gs strategic thinking, and to a wide range of external contacts to communicate our analysis and recommendations, in both written and spoken formats. Expand E3G’s relationships and networks to relevant institutions and stakeholders in trade, energy and economic security – particularly civil society organisations (CSOs), alongside government officials, research institutions, trade associations and key private sector actors, primarily in Japan and key trade partner countries, to develop productive collaborations that support achieving the programme’s objectives. In collaboration with E3G’s Japan experts and trusted partners, maintain and widen the team’s relationships with diplomats and foreign missions and trade representatives to distribute analysis and strategic advice, for example through organising and presenting in online and in-person briefings. Represent E3G externally through active participation in civil society meetings, as well as relevant conferences and other events in Japan and internationally as needed; and maintain relations to media and provide commentary and insights about their area of expertise when needed. Experience and Skills A graduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as trade policy, international relations, climate and energy policy, development, geography, or politics. A minimum of six years of relevant professional experience in a related field, such as trade, policy, research or advocacy within a government or international organisation, commercial sector, think tank, civil society or research institute. Established connections to organisations and individuals relevant for the role, e.g. government and ministries, trade associations or related research institutions, and the ability to leverage these relationships effectively and in alignment with organisational priorities. Strong analytical and strategic thinking, with an aptitude for learning new areas and consider complex information to make evidence-based recommendations. Excellent communication skills, able to convey information and arguments to others in a clear, accessible and convincing way including in sensitive or challenging stakeholder contexts. Highly organised and attention to detail, able to be proactive and deliver high-quality outputs in a timely manner. Strong interpersonal skills, with ability to form high-trust relationships with various external stakeholders and handle sensitive information with discretion, as well as patience and resilience in long-term engagement processes. Excellent written and spoken Japanese and English. Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in an international team environment. What we offer Initial contract of one year, with possibility of extension, for a full-time position. Fully remote and flexible working arrangements. 16 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Eligible for social (employee health) insurance and employment insurance. E3G offers a competitive salary and reward package which compares well with other organisations within our sector, reflecting experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. The salary shall be subject to withholdings for taxes and social and labor insurances in Japan mentioned above in which the Senior Policy Advisor will be enrolled. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G is unable to provide relocation assistance to candidates who would need to change locations in order to take up this position. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they the right to live and work in Japan. How to apply Please submit your application in English. Please include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of no more than one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please include a written description of your residency status and right to work in Japan (for example, your visa status, if applicable), in the letter. The deadline for applications is Midnight, Sunday 16th August. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we may not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us with 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

Working with others, secure funding for TBI’s health work in Africa, enabling us to expand our support to governments . Manage relationships with technical leads and focal points in partner organisations involved in co-implementation, as well as in relevant regional health organisations. Maintain relationships with technical counterparts and investment leads from institutional donors, as required. External Engagement and Partnerships Represent TBI as a senior subject-matter expert at high-profile external events, including delivering presentations Work with Africa leadership to strengthen networks and partnerships with leading health innovators and stakeholders Engage with donors, non-profit organisations, media, suppliers, and other external partners to support TBI’s strategic and financial objectives Person Specification The successful candidate will demonstrate: Extensive practical experience in the health sector in Africa, advising political leaders on complex public health and innovation challenges, or experience in government or leading advisory organisations Credibility across a wide range of health topics, with deep expertise in one or more areas. Reporting to the CTO, this role leads the Applications function, owns the platform Centre of Excellence, and provides the technical leadership that translates business needs into delivered platform capability. You will be an experienced applications leader with deep expertise in SaaS platforms, modern engineering practice (CI/CD, source control, environment and release management, test automation) and the operational realities of running mission-critical business systems globally. Excellence; platform-specific standards, delivery patterns and an internal community across the platform leads and developers Line management responsibility for the Build team Engineering Practice Own engineering practice across the Applications function: source control and repository governance (GitHub, Salesforce via Gearset), CI/CD pipelines, environment management (dev/test/UAT/prod parity and access), release management and test strategy / automation Define and enforce technical execution standards for releases, distinct from the change control approval process Define and lead engineering standards, architectural patterns and Infrastructure as Code AI Platform Operations Accountable for the operational availability of TBI's internal AI platforms (Claude, Agentforce, AI assistants) and ongoing AI consumption cost and budget management Own AI usage monitoring: drift, hallucination and misuse pattern detection, partnering with the Director of Security & Compliance, who owns AI security and the Responsible Use Policy Provide the operational foundation that enables TBI's Agentic AI and Generative AI capability pillars Capacity & Observability Own scaling (design and operation), rightsizing and optimisation of cloud and SaaS resources Own application monitoring, alerting and on-call response for in-scope platforms Lead cross-platform test strategy and quality standards Cross-Functional Working Partner with the Digital Leadership to translate business needs (the Digital Roadmap) into platform-level delivery (Platform Roadmaps) Partner with the Director of Security & Compliance on identity, access, secret management and DevSecOps practices embedded in CI/CD Partner with the Enterprise Architect on significant technical decisions and integration patterns Support the CTO with platform investment cases, vendor negotiation for strategic platforms and Executive-level reporting on platform health Person Specification Significant senior leadership experience running enterprise application functions in a mid-to-large global organisation Deep expertise in at least two of: Salesforce, Workday, and Microsoft 365 / Azure or AWS as enterprise platforms (configuration, integration, governance, licensing, support) Demonstrable experience embedding modern engineering practice incl. Role Summary TBI operates globally in politically sensitive environments, handling sensitive policy, advisory and donor information across multiple jurisdictions. Following the establishment of Cyber Essentials+ certification, a live outsourced SOC and a 24/7 monitoring posture, Digital is now entering a phase of security and compliance maturity that includes ISO 27001 ambition, AI security and governance across a rapidly expanding AI estate, and a deepened compliance posture across the regulatory regimes in which TBI operates. The Director of Security & Compliance is a new, senior role accountable for the security, governance, risk, compliance, continuity and data protection posture of TBI. Reporting to the CTO, this role leads the Security & Compliance function - the IT Security Engineer and the outsourced SOC - and provides authoritative leadership on cyber, AI and information security across the Institute. It is the named accountable owner for our certifications, our risk register, our continuity arrangements and the security and governance of our AI estate. You will be an experienced security and compliance leader with deep expertise in modern cyber operations, governance frameworks (ISO 27001 in particular), risk management and the security and governance of AI in an enterprise context. You will work closely with Legal & Risk, the Director of Applications, the Enterprise Architect and the CTO to ensure our security posture enables rather than constrains TBI's mission. Key Responsibilities Security Operations Accountable for security monitoring, incident response, remediation and security tooling / platform management across TBI (both internal and external) Own the relationship with the outsourced SOC and line manage the IT Security Engineer Own the firm-wide security awareness programme - phishing simulation, user training and security culture (delivered through a vCISO arrangement where appropriate) Own the design of identity, access (RBAC) and authentication (MFA / SSO) standards, partnering with the Global Service Desk Manager who owns day-to-day operation Governance, Risk & Compliance Own TBI's IT governance framework adoption and maintenance, including the supporting RAPID and accountability mapping Own the regulatory and standards compliance posture - GDPR, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials+, and others - including certification maintenance, control evidence, audit readiness and statutory reporting Lead TBI's path to ISO 27001 certification as a strategic programme, including the definition of certification scope across emerging functions and capabilities Own the central Digital & Data Security risk register - identification, assessment, mitigation and ongoing maintenance - in partnership with Legal & Risk Data Protection & Privacy Own the data classification framework (design and operation), data retention policies and the GDPR / data subject rights operating model Partner with Legal on the firm-wide data protection programme and breach notification process Continuity Own disaster recovery and business continuity planning, testing and recovery - including RTO / RPO definition for critical systems and the incident communications plan AI Security & Governance Own the security posture of TBI's AI estate - access and authentication for AI platforms, prompt and output data protection, prompt injection and jailbreak defence, and third-party AI vendor risk assessment (Anthropic, OpenAI, Salesforce Einstein, and others) Own TBI's Responsible Use Policy for AI tools across the firm Partner with the Director of Applications, the Enterprise Architect and the CTO to ensure all AI initiatives across TBI - including AI capability developed outside of Digital - sit within an appropriate security and governance envelope DevSecOps Own DevSecOps practice: secret management, vulnerability scanning (SAST / DAST / dependency scanning), pipeline security gates, container and workload security and code-level vulnerability management Partner with the Director of Applications to embed security controls into the engineering practice without becoming a delivery blocker Third-Party Risk Own third-party security risk assessment and ongoing vendor security monitoring, in partnership with the Head of Digital Transformation & Performance, who owns the vendor relationship and performance lifecycle Person Specification Significant senior leadership experience in security and compliance roles within a mid-to-large global organisation Deep, demonstrable expertise in ISO 27001 - ideally as named lead on a successful certification programme - together with working knowledge of SOC 2, NIST CSF and other relevant frameworks Strong technical credibility across modern security operations: SIEM, EDR, IAM, vulnerability management and DevSecOps tooling Demonstrable expertise in GDPR and data protection in a global, multi-jurisdiction context Demonstrable understanding of AI security and AI governance - prompt injection, model risk, third-party AI vendor risk and the operational realities of running an AI estate at scale Experience designing and running risk registers and risk processes at organisational level Strong stakeholder credibility at executive level; able to articulate security posture in business terms and influence non-technical audiences Pragmatic, proportionate and able to balance security rigour with delivery velocity Experience managing technical security staff and outsourced security partners Comfortable operating in politically sensitive contexts and exercising judgement on disclosure, escalation and risk acceptance Qualifications & Certifications Essential One or more of these certifications CISSP (ISC) CISM (ISACA) ISO 27001 Lead Implementer CIPP/E or CIPM (IAPP) CRISC or CGEIT (ISACA) CCSP AIGP Candidates must have the legal right to work in the UK to apply for this role. We reserve the right to close this role early if we receive a sufficient number of applications. Closing Date: 2026-08-09

Role Summary The Tony Blair Institute, in partnership with the Rwanda Development Board, is seeking to recruit an exceptional Advisor – Tourism Competitiveness & Investment Facilitation to support Rwanda’s ambition to strengthen its position as a premium, high-quality, and diversified tourism destination. This role will be embedded within the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) and will work closely with the Tourism Office, regulatory counterparts, investment facilitation teams, and wider government stakeholders. The Advisor will support two mutually reinforcing priorities: first, strengthening hospitality service quality standards, inspection practice, and enforcement credibility; and second, advancing tourism product diversification and improving the investment facilitation systems required to attract, assess, and convert high-quality tourism investments. The position will support RDB to improve the consistency and credibility of hospitality regulation through clearer service quality standards, better inspection operations, and practical enforcement improvements. In parallel, the Advisor will help the Tourism Office identify priority gaps in Rwanda’s tourism offer, build a structured pipeline of diversified tourism product opportunities, assess incoming investor proposals, and strengthen coordination across the tourism investment facilitation process. The role requires a strong delivery-oriented professional who can bridge tourism sector strategy, service quality, regulation, investment facilitation, institutional coordination, and practical implementation. The Advisor will be expected to diagnose operational and market bottlenecks, design practical tools and frameworks, support institutional adoption, and work hands-on with government teams to improve the systems that underpin tourism competitiveness, visitor experience, and investment conversion. This is not a traditional advisory role. It requires someone able to move between policy, operations, investors, and delivery; translate strategic priorities into usable tools and routines; and help RDB build stronger internal capability across both hospitality quality enforcement and tourism product development. Role Responsibilities 1. Strategic Tourism Competitiveness Advisory Advise RDB and the Tourism Office on practical interventions to strengthen Rwanda’s tourism competitiveness, with balanced attention to hospitality service quality, regulatory credibility, tourism product diversification, and investment facilitation Support the translation of Rwanda’s premium tourism positioning and NST2 tourism priorities into clear operational reforms, product opportunities, tools, and delivery plans Provide analysis on service quality gaps, regulatory bottlenecks, tourism product gaps, investor requirements, institutional coordination challenges, and implementation constraints Support RDB leadership to prioritize high-impact actions that improve the visitor experience, strengthen regulatory credibility, diversify Rwanda’s tourism offer, and improve investor confidence Prepare concise briefs, decision papers, product opportunity notes, and implementation updates for senior government and RDB stakeholders 2. Hospitality Service Quality Standards & Regulation Conduct a rapid diagnostic of current hospitality inspection, classification, and enforcement practices to identify key gaps, bottlenecks, and root causes Support the design of a tiered hospitality service quality standards framework covering facilities, service delivery, and staff conduct Develop practical tools that can be used by both hospitality operators and inspectors as a clear compliance reference and objective inspection benchmark Develop an inspection operations guide setting out how inspections should be planned, conducted, documented, escalated, and followed up Identify quick wins and prepare a short-term enforcement improvement roadmap to strengthen inspection consistency, regulatory credibility, and service quality follow-through 3. Tourism Product Diversification & Pipeline Development Support RDB’s Tourism Office to develop a structured tourism product diversification pipeline aligned with NST2 priorities and Rwanda’s premium destination positioning Map Rwanda’s current tourism product offer and identify priority gaps and opportunities across high-value and emerging tourism segments Develop a framework for prioritizing tourism product opportunities based on strategic fit, market demand, investor appetite, feasibility, geographic spread, contribution to length of stay, and alignment with national targets Support the Tourism Office to convert priority product categories into clear opportunity concepts and investor-facing propositions Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of tourism product opportunities, including new concepts, active investor leads, proposals under assessment, and opportunities requiring cross-government support 4. Tourism Investment Facilitation & Investor Assessment Design a front-end investor assessment framework enabling the Tourism Office to evaluate investor seriousness, strategic fit, and project quality at the earliest stage of engagement Assess incoming tourism investment proposals against agreed criteria, including investor seriousness, product quality, destination fit, commercial viability, sustainability, and potential contribution to Rwanda’s tourism objectives Develop an investor journey and decision-point guide clarifying roles, responsibilities, handover points, and escalation channels across RDB departments and partner agencies Develop and operationalise an investment monitoring tracker to record investor interactions, assessment outcomes, pipeline status, and next steps Support follow-through on priority investor engagements, ensuring that bottlenecks are identified, escalated, and resolved in a timely manner 5. Coordination, Institutional Strengthening & Capacity Building Establish a coordination embedding toolkit, including standardized templates, escalation protocols, and operating procedures for both tourism investment facilitation and quality service follow-through Strengthening coordination between the Tourism Office, investment facilitation teams, regulatory counterparts, and relevant partner agencies Design and deliver capacity-building sessions to equip Tourism Office staff and relevant counterparts to use the service quality tools, investor assessment framework, coordination protocols, and monitoring tracker independently Support regular review routines with RDB teams to track progress, unblock constraints, and maintain delivery discipline across both workstreams Contribute to embedding a more data-driven, results-oriented, service-quality-focused, and investor-responsive culture within the relevant RDB teams Candidate Profile 10+ years of relevant experience in tourism development, hospitality, destination competitiveness, investment facilitation, private sector development, public sector delivery, management consulting, or a related field Strong understanding of tourism competitiveness, including hospitality service quality, regulatory systems, inspection practices, tourism product development, and investor facilitation Demonstrated experience designing Role Summary The Tony Blair Institute is recruiting an Analyst to provide research, analytical, and delivery support to TBI's embedded advisory teams working across Government of Rwanda institutions and the Country Director's Office. This is a generalist, entry-level role: the Analyst will be assigned to a specific project area based on Country Office and project team needs — which may span trade, investment, tourism, public finance, skills development, or other areas of Government priority — and will work closely with the Advisor or Manager leading that workstream, as well as the Country Director's Office. No prior sector specialisation is required. The Analyst will bring strong foundational skills in research, data analysis, data, coordination, together with a can-do attitude, and will be expected to build sector-specific knowledge quickly on the job. This role suits an intellectually curious, structured, delivery-oriented early-career professional with a genuine willingness to learn, looking to build a career in government advisory or public sector delivery. Role Responsibilities 1. Research, Analysis & Data Support Conduct research and analysis, both quantitative and qualitative, to inform project deliverables and decision-making Collect, clean, and organise data from government and other sources; carry out basic analysis such as trend identification, comparisons, and benchmarking Support the development of simple tools, trackers, and models to monitor project indicators and progress Perform quality control on data and analytical outputs to ensure accuracy and validity 2. Material Development & Communication Draft high-quality briefing notes, concept notes, presentations, and other materials for senior leadership in government and TBI Support the preparation of decision papers, workshop materials, and stakeholder-facing documents Synthesise complex information into clear, structured, and actionable outputs 3. Coordination and Delivery Support Support planning, scheduling, and coordination of activities across project workstreams and the Country Office Track action items, deadlines, and follow-ups, flagging risks, delays, or bottlenecks to the Senior Advisor/Manager in a timely manner Organize meetings, workshops, and stakeholder engagements across projects and the Country Office, including logistics and follow-up Develop and maintain working relationships with government counterparts and project stakeholders Contribute to periodic reporting on project and Country Office performance, indicators, and outcomes Candidate Profile University degree in Economics, Business, Public Policy, Law, Engineering, Social Sciences, or a related field 0–2 years of relevant experience, with internships, research assistantships, or early-career roles in consulting, government, development, or the private sector welcomed Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with basic exposure to quantitative and qualitative research and policy analysis Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word Ability to draft clear briefing notes, presentations, and materials for senior audiences, and synthesise complex information into actionable outputs; some exposure to project coordination or multi-stakeholder environments (e.g. internships, student groups) is an advantage Excellent written and verbal communication, strong organisation and attention to detail, sound judgement handling sensitive information, and learning agility with openness to feedback and coaching Capabilities and Ways of Working Agility & Comfort with Ambiguity Adapts quickly to shifting priorities and new information Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving government environment Brings structure and clarity to unfamiliar problems Builds & Broadens Builds effective working relationships across teams and counterparts Proactively seeks feedback and continuously builds knowledge across sectors Shares learning and contributes positively to a growing team Collaboration, Integrity & Trust Operates with professionalism, discretion, and sound judgement Collaborates effectively across levels and disciplines Communicates clearly and constructively Drive & Delivery Maintains a strong focus on quality and timely delivery Takes ownership of assigned tasks and follows through Shows persistence and resourcefulness when facing challenges What Success Looks Like (6-12 Months) Delivers high-quality, timely research, analysis, and materials that are used directly by senior advisors and government counterparts Builds working sector knowledge relevant to the assigned project area(s), reducing the need for close oversight over time Maintains accurate, up-to-date tracking and monitoring tools that support team reporting and decision-making Demonstrates growing confidence and capability engaging with stakeholders and coordinating delivery across workstreams Is recognised by the team as a reliable, detail-oriented contributor able to take on increasing responsibility Closing Date: 2026-08-10
